extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers preparing NIH K99/R00 Pathway to Independence grant applications (and their mentors/administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A sample NIH K99/R00 Pathway to Independence application demonstrating required career development plan, specific aims, research strategy (including pilot RCT), measures, recruitment, power justification, and benchmarks across K99 (training) and R00 (independence) phases. Intended to guide postdocs on designing and documenting a competitive K99/R00 submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although these applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grantees applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use validated or objective measures whenever possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible we will use validated or objective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, for some outcomes, no validated measures exist. In these cases, draw upon measures used in the published literature, develop measures based on published recommendations, or develop measures tailored to the project (to be validated in future studies). Table 5 lists proposed measures and schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training success threshold (feasibility measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Success of training will be assessed by 70% or greater endorsement of each feasibility measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility measures include utility of individual modules and training appropriateness and fit within organizational culture; used to decide iterative revisions in Aim 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register pilot RCT on ClinicalTrials.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: We will register this pilot RCT on ClinicalTrials.gov so that other researchers may reproduce and extend our findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration supports transparency and reproducibility of the pilot efficacy test (Aim 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Achieve thematic saturation in qualitative data
rubrics_metrics.description: For qualitative methods, we believe sample sizes will be sufficient to obtain thematic saturation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, continue to collect data at all stages until thematic saturation is achieved; record and transcribe interviews and code transcriptions for themes using responsive interviewing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use modified Delphi with stakeholders until consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a modified Delphi approach, soliciting multiple rounds of structured feedback from a team of key stakeholders until consensus is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders include hospice clinicians, African American and white family caregivers, and content/research experts. Circulate feedback among stakeholders, request return within 4 weeks, compile responses, and follow-up with a 30–60 minute interview within 2 weeks for additional feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate tool with think-aloud strategy and qualitative interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the tool using a 'think aloud' strategy with family caregivers and hospice clinicians followed by qualitative interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After each think-aloud exercise participants complete a 15–20 minute qualitative interview to confirm and clarify findings. Participants assess feasibility including cultural inclusiveness, usability, and perceived utility. Use iterative two-stage testing and modify training/tool after each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot testing sample size guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recommended sample sizes for feasibility and pilot testing (Aim 3 and Aim 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 3: pilot training with two groups of 10 hospice clinicians (n=20); pilot the tool with two groups of 15 (5 clinicians, 5 African American FCG, 5 white FCG) (total n=30). Aim 4: pilot test preliminary efficacy with 40 hospice clinicians (grouped to n≈20 per arm) and 160 family caregivers (80 African American, 80 white). Rationale: 10–30 participants are adequate for this type of feasibility/usability testing; power calculation for 160 FCG gives OR=2.33 with power 0.82 at α=0.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use randomized controlled trial design for preliminary efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) to determine preliminary efficacy of the training and tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomly assign clinician groups to intervention or control; deliver intervention as in-service sessions during team meetings; control receives an in-service presentation on patterns of hospice use among PwD. Primary purpose of pilot is directionality and effect size estimates for a future fully-powered RCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes for efficacy testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcomes include: (1) improve hospice clinicians' knowledge about dementia caregiving at EOL; (2) reduce family caregiver (FCG) burden; (3) reduce people with dementia (PwD) hospice disenrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clinicians' knowledge before and after in-service; assess FCG burden prior to clinician visits up to four times; verify hospice discharge status via electronic hospice records at 3 and 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific validated measures where available
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed measures include the Zarit Caregiver Burden Inventory (12), Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale, GAS Score, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All measures in Table 5 will be assessed via self-report; verify discharge status using electronic hospice records. Use validated measures where possible and psychometrically justify chosen instruments; where measures are TBD, develop items and validate in future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative coding and consensus procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative analysis: trained raters will independently review transcripts and identify passages that include suggestions for inclusion and/or modifications to the intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raters organize passages into theme categories, discuss themes, and make revisions until consensus is reached regarding themes. Identified themes will inform modifications to intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative analysis and modeling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative analysis: calculate descriptive statistics to characterize samples; calculate changes by comparing individual responses over time; use logistic regression for preliminary efficacy analyses with main predictor participation in intervention vs control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outcome variables described in section C7 (dichotomous measures of clinician knowledge improvement, FCG stress reduction, hospice disenrollment). Pilot sample sizes provide directionality and effect-size estimates for future R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a Biological Variable monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will not be excluded based on sex or gender; recruitment rates across sex/gender will be monitored to minimize selection biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given that over 60% of FCG and 72% of hospice clinicians are female, expect majority female participants. If a patient sex/gender is under-represented (<30%), modify recruitment strategies to target the under-represented group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks for career-development success
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks include obtaining 4 publications, presenting annually at national conferences, having sufficient data for a competitive R01, and launching as an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks tied to K99 (training/product development) and R00 (pilot testing/preliminary efficacy) outputs and career transition milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitize final tool using CREATE usability protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: We will create manuals for each and digitize the final tool using CREATE protocols for user-centered design and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess usability in real-world hospice settings using Dr. Czaja's CREATE usability protocols; incorporate usability findings into final tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Goal Attainment Scaling (GAS) for goal assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a GAS-based tool for hospice clinicians and family caregivers to set goals and outcomes for dementia-related care and support needs at EOL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAS uses a -2 to +2 scale (sample goals and outcomes provided). GAS has precedent in measuring treatment effects and case resolution; adapt and pilot-test GAS in hospice setting and diverse populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize recruitment of underrepresented groups with community partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize African American recruitment over white subjects when needed; engage physicians, community partners, and experts to assist recruitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with WCM-NYP physicians and community partners (letters of support referenced). Seek input from recruitment experts and letters of support from organizations like CaringKind and VNSNY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility criteria for intervention products
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 3 outcomes: the training and tool should be culturally inclusive and practical for incorporation into hospice care delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility and acceptability measured via participant feedback in interactive sessions and think-aloud exercises; modifications made iteratively to produce a final training and digitized tool for Aim 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed timeline and milestones across K99/R00 phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a research timeline outlining activities across quarters for K99 and R00 years (startup, Aim 1 interviews/survey, Aim 2 develop training/tool, Aim 3 feasibility testing, Aim 4 preliminary efficacy testing, manuscript preparation, and R00/R01 applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Table 6 to demonstrate realistic scheduling of IRB approval, recruitment, data collection, analysis, and dissemination benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate rigor and address research gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify use of rigorous methods (e.g., RCT) and explain how the project addresses gaps in existing literature (e.g., lack of research on PwD in home hospice and African American PwD/FCG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior work, explain methodological choices, and show how pilot data will enable fully-powered RCTs and reproducibility (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov registration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate challenges and provide alternative approaches/mitigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify likely challenges (e.g., recruitment difficulties, limited budget/timeframe preventing web-based training, choice of GAS) and provide concrete responses/contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include engaging community partners to assist recruitment, prioritizing African American recruitment, and testing alternative approaches in future studies when resources allow.
